cohort: The study included 621 nulliparous patients with confirmed pregnancies who received prenatal care at a large medical center between 2006 and 2022.
finding: A retroverted uterus is associated with a higher likelihood of requiring in vitro fertilization (IVF) but does not significantly impact pregnancy complications or vaginal delivery outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery rates were comparable between patients with anteverted and retroverted uteri among those attempting vaginal delivery.
